title: Annotatio I §.III close: Not all Institution words tropic from the Cup; yet sacramentals do not abhor impropriety — Disparatum as grave cause
pass_a_gloss: So in turn he will have me consenting to him in a double way — both that from the admitted impropriety of the said proposition (This cup is the N.T. in my blood) it does not follow that all the remaining words pertaining to the Institution of the Sacred Eucharist are to be taken tropically; and that the proper sense of words is everywhere to be retained unless a grave cause obstructs — provided Dom. Scultetus will not be unwilling further to observe (1) that I have not wished, nor do I still wish, to infer from this improper proposition This cup is the New Testament that all the words of the Institution of the Sacred Supper are improper, but only to say: Definitive Sacramentals so little abhor impropriety that from the impropriety of all of them in general (excepting for a while only these: This is my body), to be admitted without controversy, the impropriety of these too can at least most probably be inferred. (2) That the impropriety just named must necessarily be transcribed to these last, because a most grave cause obstructs their propriety — than which none graver can be given — namely that otherwise it will come about that a Disparate must be said to be predicated properly of a Disparate, against all the nature of this and sound human reason.
pass_b_english: So Strimesius consents on two points: admitting Cup impropriety does not make every other Institution word tropical; and proper sense stays unless a grave cause blocks it.

(1) He does not infer from This cup is the New Testament that all Supper Institution words are improper — only that definitive sacramentals so little abhor impropriety that from all the rest (This is my body set aside for now) one may most probably infer these too are improper.

(2) That impropriety must be written onto This is my body as well, because the gravest cause blocks propriety: otherwise a Disparate would have to be predicated properly of a Disparate against nature and sound reason.
source_text: Ita vicissim me sibi duplici modo habuerit consentientem, tùm quod ex dictae propositionis (Hoc poculum est N. T. in sanguine meo) improprietate admissâ, non sequatur, omnia reliqua, ad S. Eucharistiae institutionem pertinentia verba, tropicè sumenda; tùm quòd proprius verborum sensus ubivis retinendus sit, nisi gravis obstet causa; dummodo praetereà observare haud gravetur Dominus Scultetus (1) me non ex propositione impropria hac: Hoc poculum est Novum Testamentum, inferre vel voluisse, vel etiamnum velle, omnia S. Coenae institutionis verba impropria esse, sed dicere duntaxat: Definitiva Sacramentalia adeo non abhorrere ab improprietate, ut ex omnium in universum (exceptis tantisper his solis; Hoc est corpus meum) improprietate, citra controversiam admittenda, probabilissimè saltem, & horum inferri queat improprietas. (2) Dictam modò improprietatem, postremis hisce necessariò transcribendam esse, quòd gravissima proprietati eorum causa obstet, quâ gravior dari nequit, ea scil. qua alioquin futurum est, ut Disparatum de Disparato, contra omnem hujus naturam sanamque hominum rationem, propriè praedicari dicendum fuerit.

rejected: not abhor from impropriety of manners

notes: Strimesius (1)(2); Disparatum as grave cause; §.III close.
